title: Make the existing binding index support the exact bounded event order
summary: Follow-up to merged CURRENT source delivery PR #6525 (commit 9624c19d7 -> 714289cf8) and blocked ACTUAL-TIMEOUT/gen2 PR #6526. The actual rb248 binding whole factory at limit 100 and 50 still timed out under 5.0s because PostgreSQL had to scan 194,975 index TIDs and 194,969 qualified rows with 225,552 lossy bitmap rechecks per worker and sort all rows before taking LIMIT 100/50 (diagnostic EXPLAIN ANALYZE BUFFERS completed in 16.763s total / 16.656s execution time; diagnostic receipt: /tmp/pantheon-full-closeout-20261011/original-failed-9624-SQL-bounded-EXPLAIN-ANALYZE-diagnostic-NOT-CAPACITY-PASS.json). Unbounded heap and sort access was demonstrated on the existing index. While only a simplified four-row/enable_seqscan=off local case was tested locally and not the actual 714 full factory, defining covering ordered index idx_telemetry_events_binding_id_created_at_ingested_seq on ((payload->>'binding_id'), created_at DESC, ingested_seq DESC) in scripts/db_migrate.sh and retiring legacy root-only idx_telemetry_events_binding_id provides the proposed mechanism and local ordering-support proof. Existing merged 714 reader SQL, strict typed binding/runtime guards, tenant isolation, and deterministic tie-breaker semantics remain completely unchanged. Production net growth is exactly +9 lines in scripts/db_migrate.sh against dev base 714289cf8 (budget <= 20). Tests cover fresh schema migration, old schema upgrade, idempotency, and exact ordering / tie behavior with 14 passed in test_db_migrate.py and 146 passed across 4 telemetry/incident test suites. Source delivery prepared pending review, CI, and merge; actual hosted 5s / FULL / healthy Loop10 capacity remains unverified and pending delivery, with coordinator owning migration apply and hosted capacity verification.

cause_and_solution_proof.demonstrated_defect: PostgreSQL query planner was forced to perform Bitmap Index Scan on idx_telemetry_events_binding_id returning 194,975 index TIDs and 194,969 qualified rows, followed by Gather and top-N Sort over all 194,969 rows before taking LIMIT 100, because the legacy index only indexed (payload->>'binding_id') without ordering columns created_at DESC, ingested_seq DESC.
cause_and_solution_proof.solution_mechanism: Added covering ordered expression index idx_telemetry_events_binding_id_created_at_ingested_seq ON telemetry_events ((payload->>'binding_id'), created_at DESC, ingested_seq DESC) in scripts/db_migrate.sh and retired redundant root-only idx_telemetry_events_binding_id. In local disposable PostgreSQL testing with enable_seqscan=off on simplified four-row case, the index demonstrates local ordering-support proof for the proposed mechanism (Index Scan in created_at DESC, ingested_seq DESC order without Sort node). Actual hosted planner behavior on full factory and actual hosted 5s / FULL / healthy Loop10 capacity remain unverified and pending delivery/coordinator apply.
cause_and_solution_proof.lifecycle_and_lock_behavior: The ordered replacement index is created first with CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS (acquires SHARE lock on telemetry_events, permitting concurrent SELECT reads). Once verified, the redundant root-only index is retired via DROP INDEX IF EXISTS. In case of migration failure, transaction halts before drop, ensuring continuous index coverage. Migration is fully idempotent across fresh, pre-existing, and repeated executions.
